predecessors.name: Russian Republic
predecessors.text: Transcaucasia, governed from Tiflis by the Transcaucasian Commissariat (established 15 November 1917) and its Seim (23 February 1918) before the federation was proclaimed

successors.name: Georgia
successors.text: the Georgian members proclaimed the Democratic Republic of Georgia on 26 May 1918

ledger.x: 1918, 22 April: the Seim proclaims Transcaucasia an independent federative republic at Tiflis.
1918, April: the Ottoman army holds Batum and presses on Kars.
1918, 26 May: the Seim dissolves and the Georgian members proclaim the Democratic Republic of Georgia.
1918, 28 May: Armenia declares independence, 'two days later' than 26 May.
1918, 28 May: Azerbaijan proclaims its independence the same day as Armenia.
1918, 26-28 May: the war passes to the successors.

wars.name: Caucasus campaign
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory on the ground: Batum taken on 14 April, Kars surrendered on 25 April; the offensive resumed on 21 May stalled at Sardarabad, Bash Abaran and Kara Killisse; the federation dissolved on 26-28 May and its successors signed the Treaty of Batum on…

certainty.note: No frontier of the federation was fixed by treaty: the Brest-Litovsk cession of Ardahan, Batum and Kars was refused, the Trabzon and Batum conferences produced only a draft, and the outlines are the successors' Cliopatria shapes.
